body:
Fixed in 9e06d40: the embedded Khronos loader now also scans /run/opengl-driver/share for ICD manifests — the path where NixOS publishes them, and which nixpkgs patches into its own vulkan-loader. A build from master should render; the fix will be in the next release binary.

The broader point is worth stating: NixOS support of this kind requires explicit action from anyone who statically links a Vulkan loader, because the upstream loader only searches FHS paths that NixOS deliberately does not have. And loading the system's libvulkan.so.1 dynamically does not save you either — on NixOS there is no ld.so.cache and no /usr/lib, so a foreign binary simply cannot find the .so on disk; the distribution's layout knowledge lives in its own patched loader and in the RPATHs of nix-built executables. Until then, VK_DRIVER_FILES=/run/opengl-driver/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.x86_64.json also works as a manual override with the current binary.

Superseded by 3a5cbc4d on main — upstream landed the same fix (GCC's LINK_EH_SPEC drops --eh-frame-hdr for -static; pass the flag on the static links) while this PR was in flight, together with the empty-auxv guard. Closing as redundant. Our repro confirmed the same failure mode: pre-fix, ./build test aborted at tst/smoke.cpp:285.

Thanks for the report and the diagnosis — dotnet's self-location genuinely breaks under solo run. But intercepting path strings in the bridge is a direction we can't take, so I'll decline this approach. Here is why it cannot be made to work:

The surface is unbounded. readlink, readlinkat, and realpath are three of many readers of /proc/self/exe. The same answer is reachable through open() — a single-file dotnet bundle reads itself by opening /proc/self/exe — stat/fstatat, fopen, /proc/<pid>/exe with the process's own pid, a dirfd-relative openat(fd_of_proc_self, "exe"), and std::filesystem. Every one of those is another strcmp patch, forever.

Raw syscalls bypass the bridge entirely. The bridge only sees what routes through a guest's glibc imports. CoreCLR and Go-style runtimes issue direct syscalls; those get the kernel's answer no matter what the bridge says.

The lie cannot be made consistent. After this patch, readlink("/proc/self/exe") names the guest while open/stat of the same path, /proc/self/maps, and /proc/self/status still name solo. A runtime that cross-checks — and runtimes do — now sees a contradictory world, which is worse than the honest one. Userspace string-matching can't fix that; only the kernel can.

It's the wrong layer for this project. The bridge adapts the glibc ABI onto musl and fails loudly where it can't; it does not silently alter kernel semantics based on which path string a call carries. Once that door opens, the bridge starts growing toward fakeroot.

The place where /proc/self/exe is already correct is interpreter mode: when the kernel execs the guest with solo as its PT_INTERP, the exe link, the maps, the auxv, and the stack are all truthful with zero patches — for libc calls and raw syscalls alike. That's the supported way to run self-locating guests today, and it needs no changes to solo:

cp dotnet dotnet-solo
patchelf --set-interpreter /absolute/path/to/solo dotnet-solo
./dotnet-solo --info

(PT_INTERP must be an absolute path; patch a copy so the original stays runnable on glibc hosts. readelf -lW dotnet-solo | grep interpreter confirms the change.)

Could solo run itself get there — stop emulating execve, and instead have the kernel do it through a namespace trick that plants solo at the path the guest's PT_INTERP names? We'll think about it, but that solution carries its own set of problems — the same ones nix-ld struggles with: the planted interpreter is inherited by every child the guest spawns, including ordinary glibc binaries that expected the real ld.so; user namespaces are unavailable or restricted in many containers and hardened kernels; and namespace tricks break setuid. So for now the patchelf route above is the answer.
